title: Exile group reveals secret sites at Natanz and Arak
detail: At a press conference in Washington the National Council of Resistance of Iran said Iran was building a nuclear fuel plant at Natanz and a heavy-water plant at Arak. Iran later declared both to the IAEA.
source_name: NCRI remarks (Alireza Jafarzadeh), transcript via Iran Watch
notes: Opposition group with an interest in the story; press reports say US agencies already knew of the sites.

title: IAEA chief visits Natanz; Iran declares enrichment plant
detail: IAEA Director General ElBaradei visited Iran in February 2003; Iran declared the Natanz enrichment plants under construction, and inspectors saw the pilot plant.
notes: Visit 21-22 February 2003 as recorded in the IAEA report.

title: Weapons work (AMAD plan) halted, IAEA later finds
detail: The IAEA's final assessment says a coordinated programme of activities relevant to a nuclear explosive device, the AMAD plan, was brought to a halt in late 2003; some activities continued to 2009.
notes: Date is 'late 2003' (US 2007 NIE: 'fall 2003'); placed at 1 October 2003 by convention, day and month not known.

title: Tehran Declaration with Britain, France and Germany
detail: Iran agreed with the three European foreign ministers to sign the Additional Protocol and to suspend enrichment voluntarily while talks went on.
notes: The agreed statement of 21 Oct 2003 is quoted in footnote 2 of the IAEA's November 2003 report.

title: Iran admits earlier enrichment tests with uranium gas
detail: The IAEA reported that Iran had acknowledged testing centrifuges with UF6 at the Kalaye Electric Company workshop between 1998 and 2002, undeclared at the time: Iran's first enrichment.
source_name: IAEA, GOV/2003/75 (10 November 2003), paras 16 and following
notes: Iran's letter of 21 Oct 2003 (para 16) says 1998-2002; Iranian officials elsewhere said 1999 and 2002. Dated to the IAEA report.

title: Paris agreement: enrichment suspension takes effect
detail: Under the Paris agreement of 15 November 2004 with the E3, Iran suspended enrichment-related and conversion activities; the IAEA verified the suspension as of 22 November.
notes: Agreement text: INFCIRC/637 (iaea.org, not fetched: site blocks automated access).

title: Iran ends suspension, restarts uranium conversion at Isfahan
detail: Iran began feeding uranium ore concentrate into the Isfahan conversion plant on 8 August and removed IAEA seals on 10 August, ending the Paris suspension for conversion.

title: Iran tells IAEA Board the Leader has forbidden nuclear weapons
detail: At an emergency Board meeting Iran's delegation said the Leader had issued a fatwa that the production, stockpiling and use of nuclear weapons are forbidden under Islam.
source_name: IRNA text (10 Aug 2005), reproduced by Juan Cole, Informed Comment
notes: Read on the evening of Tuesday 9 Aug 2005 (IRNA dispatch dated 10 Aug). See fatwa.csv.

title: IAEA Board finds Iran in non-compliance
detail: The Board found that Iran's failures and breaches of its safeguards obligations constituted non-compliance.

title: Iran resumes enrichment research
detail: Iran told the IAEA it would resume, from 9 January 2006, the research it had suspended voluntarily.

title: IAEA Board reports Iran to the Security Council
detail: The Board asked the Director General to report to the UN Security Council on Iran.

title: First enrichment to 3.6% at Natanz pilot plant
detail: Iran declared to the IAEA that its 164-machine cascade had reached 3.6% enrichment; IAEA samples tended to confirm it. President Ahmadinejad had announced the step on 11 April.
notes: Public announcement 11 April 2006; declaration to IAEA 13 April.

title: UN Resolution 1696 demands suspension
detail: The Security Council demanded that Iran suspend all enrichment-related and reprocessing activities.

title: UN Resolution 1737: first UN sanctions
detail: The Council imposed the first UN sanctions: a ban on supplying nuclear and missile items and an asset freeze on listed people and entities.

title: Natanz commercial-scale plant starts enriching
detail: Iran began feeding uranium gas into the first cascades of the underground Fuel Enrichment Plant at Natanz.
notes: Month only (February 2007); day 01 by convention. URL not fetched (IAEA site blocks automated access).

title: UN Resolution 1747 widens sanctions
detail: The Council banned Iranian arms exports and widened the asset freeze.

title: US estimate: Iran halted weapons work in fall 2003
detail: The National Intelligence Estimate judged with high confidence that in fall 2003 Tehran halted its nuclear weapons design and weaponization work, and that it had not restarted as of mid-2007.
source_name: ODNI, NIE 'Iran: Nuclear Intentions and Capabilities' (key judgments), copy via Iran Watch
notes: Official copy at dni.gov (blocks automated access).

title: UN Resolution 1803 adds travel bans and inspections
detail: The Council added travel bans, a ban on dual-use goods and cargo inspections.

title: UN Resolution 1835 reaffirms demands
detail: The Council reaffirmed its earlier resolutions without new measures.

title: US threat assessment: halt confirmed, option kept open
detail: The DNI repeated that weapon design and weaponization work was halted in fall 2003 and said Iranian entities continue to develop capabilities that could be applied to producing weapons.
source_name: DNI Dennis Blair, Annual Threat Assessment, SSCI (12 February 2009), copy via Iran Watch

title: Iran discloses Fordow enrichment plant near Qom
detail: Iran told the IAEA by letter that it was building a second enrichment plant, at Fordow; the US, Britain and France made it public on 25 September.
notes: Conflict: Iran's letter is dated 21 Sept 2009; an IAEA news item says declared 24 Sept. Public disclosure by Obama, Brown and Sarkozy at Pittsburgh on 25 Sept (not separately sourced here).

title: Physicist Masoud Alimohammadi killed in Tehran
detail: A bomb killed the Tehran University physicist; Iran blamed Israel and the United States, which denied it.
notes: Attribution never officially acknowledged.

title: Iran starts enriching to 20%
detail: Iran began feeding low-enriched uranium into a cascade at the Natanz pilot plant to make uranium enriched up to 20%, saying it was for research-reactor fuel.

title: Khamenei message: use of nuclear weapons is haram
detail: In a message to Tehran's disarmament conference Khamenei said Iran considered the use of nuclear and other weapons of mass destruction haram (forbidden).
notes: Registered at the UN as A/64/752-S/2010/203. See fatwa.csv.

title: UN Resolution 1929: broadest UN sanctions
detail: The Council banned Iranian investment in sensitive nuclear activities abroad, ballistic-missile work and heavy-arms sales to Iran, and tightened financial and shipping measures.

title: Stuxnet computer worm made public
detail: A worm that targeted industrial control systems, later linked to Natanz's centrifuges, was found by a Belarusian security firm in mid-June 2010 and reported publicly in mid-July.
notes: Discovered mid-June 2010 (VirusBlokAda); first public post 12 July. Attribution to the US and Israel rests on press reports, never officially acknowledged.

title: Fuel loading begins at Bushehr power reactor
detail: Russian and Iranian technicians began loading Russian-supplied fuel into Iran's first power reactor at Bushehr.
notes: Fuel went into the reactor core later (Oct 2010); grid connection Sept 2011 (not sourced here).

title: Car bombs kill Majid Shahriari, wound Fereydoon Abbasi
detail: Bombs attached to cars killed nuclear engineer Shahriari and wounded scientist Abbasi in Tehran.
notes: Iran blamed Israel and the US.

title: Gunmen kill Darioush Rezaeinejad in Tehran
detail: Gunmen on motorcycles shot Rezaeinejad; Iran's intelligence minister later said he had no nuclear role.
notes: His link to the programme is disputed.

title: IAEA annex sets out evidence of weapons work
detail: The IAEA's annex on possible military dimensions described information that Iran had carried out activities relevant to a nuclear explosive device, including at Parchin.
notes: IAEA assessment, not an intelligence agency; kind 'intelligence' used for assessments of weapons work.

title: Fordow starts enriching
detail: Iran began feeding uranium enriched up to 5% into two linked cascades at Fordow to make 20% uranium.

title: US NDAA section 1245 targets Iran's central bank
detail: The defence authorisation act for 2012 required sanctions on foreign banks dealing with Iran's central bank unless their countries significantly cut Iranian oil purchases.
source_name: Public Law 112-81, National Defense Authorization Act for FY2012, sec. 1245
notes: Signed 31 December 2011.

title: Magnetic bomb kills Natanz official Mostafa Ahmadi Roshan
detail: Assailants on a motorcycle attached a bomb to the car of the chemist, a Natanz official, killing him and his driver.
notes: Fourth killing in two years; Iran blamed Israel and the US.

title: EU adopts embargo on Iranian oil
detail: The EU banned new contracts to import Iranian crude and petroleum products, with existing contracts allowed to run until 1 July 2012, and froze central bank assets.
source_name: EU Official Journal, Council Decision 2012/35/CFSP (23 January 2012)

title: US threat assessment: Iran keeping option open
detail: The DNI said Iran was keeping open the option to develop nuclear weapons but 'we do not know, however, if Iran will eventually decide to build nuclear weapons.'
source_name: DNI James Clapper, Worldwide Threat Assessment, SSCI (31 January 2012)
notes: Same 'we do not know if' sentence in the 12 March 2013 statement.

title: Khamenei: Iran 'will never pursue' nuclear weapons
detail: Meeting nuclear officials and scientists, Khamenei said Iran had never pursued and would never pursue nuclear weapons and that possessing them was a great sin.
notes: Translations vary ('great', 'big' or 'grave' sin).

title: Iranian banks cut off from SWIFT
detail: After an EU Council decision of 15 March, the SWIFT messaging network disconnected EU-sanctioned Iranian banks, effective 17 March 2012.
notes: Legal basis Council Decision 2012/152/CFSP (15 March); Regulation 267/2012 followed on 23 March.

title: EU oil embargo fully in force
detail: The wind-down period for existing contracts ended, so EU imports of Iranian oil stopped.

title: Advanced IR-2m centrifuges installed at Natanz
detail: The IAEA reported that Iran had begun installing IR-2m centrifuges, its first advanced model in production use, at the Natanz Fuel Enrichment Plant.
notes: Dated to the report; installation began in early 2013. URL not fetched (IAEA site blocks automated access).

title: US threat assessment: no decision known
detail: 'We do not know if Iran will eventually decide to build nuclear weapons,' the DNI said, adding that Iran had the capacity to produce them eventually.
source_name: DNI James Clapper, Worldwide Threat Assessment, SSCI (12 March 2013)

title: Interim deal (Joint Plan of Action) agreed in Geneva
detail: Iran and the P5+1 agreed a six-month first step: Iran would stop enriching above 5%, dilute or convert its 20% stock and accept more inspections, for limited sanctions relief.
notes: Agreed in the early hours of 24 Nov in Geneva (fact sheet dated 23 Nov, US time). Implementation began 20 Jan 2014.

title: Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action agreed in Vienna
detail: Iran and the P5+1 agreed limits on enrichment, stock and centrifuges for 10-15 years, with IAEA monitoring, in return for the lifting of nuclear sanctions.

title: UN Resolution 2231 endorses the deal
detail: The Council endorsed the JCPOA and set out how UN sanctions would end, and the snapback procedure to restore them.

title: IAEA chief visits Parchin building
detail: IAEA chief Amano visited the Parchin building, where the agency had seen extensive alteration since it first asked for access in 2012; he saw no chamber, and samples did not support Iran's account of its use.
notes: Imagery supported a large cylindrical object at the site in 2000 (para 56). IAEA assessment.

title: IAEA final assessment of past weapons work
detail: Activities relevant to a nuclear explosive device were conducted as a coordinated effort before the end of 2003, some after; they did not go beyond feasibility and scientific studies; no credible indications after 2009.
notes: IAEA assessment.

title: Implementation Day: deal takes effect, sanctions lifted
detail: The IAEA verified that Iran had taken the steps required by the deal, triggering the lifting of nuclear-related UN, EU and US sanctions.
notes: URL not fetched (IAEA site blocks automated access); confirmed in search index.

title: Mossad seizes Iran's nuclear archive in Tehran
detail: Israeli agents took about 100,000 documents and files on the AMAD weapons project from a warehouse in Tehran's Shorabad district; Netanyahu revealed it on 30 April 2018.
source_name: Netanyahu presentation transcript (30 April 2018), via Iran Watch
notes: Seizure date 31 Jan 2018 from later reporting; one source (Jewish Virtual Library) says January 2017.

title: US threat assessment: deal lengthened breakout to a year
detail: The DNI said the deal had extended the time Iran needed to produce enough fissile material for a weapon from a few months to about one year, as long as Iran kept to it.
source_name: Washington Times, 13 February 2018 (quoting DNI Coats's assessment)
notes: Primary PDF not fetched (blocked).

title: Netanyahu unveils seized nuclear archive
detail: Netanyahu presented documents he said showed Project AMAD aimed to design, build and test nuclear weapons.
source_name: Netanyahu presentation transcript, via Iran Watch

title: United States leaves the nuclear deal
detail: President Trump ended US participation in the JCPOA and ordered US nuclear sanctions re-imposed after 90- and 180-day wind-downs.

title: US oil and banking sanctions re-imposed
detail: Treasury designated more than 700 people, entities, aircraft and vessels as the oil, shipping and banking sanctions returned.
source_name: US Treasury press release sm541 (5 November 2018)
notes: Eight countries got temporary oil waivers.

title: US threat assessment: no key weapons work
detail: 'We continue to assess that Iran is not currently undertaking the key nuclear weapons-development activities we judge necessary to produce a nuclear device.'
source_name: VOA, 29 January 2019 (DNI Coats, Worldwide Threat Assessment)
notes: Primary PDF not fetched (senate.gov blocks).

title: US ends oil waivers
detail: The waivers that let eight buyers keep importing Iranian oil expired on 2 May, as announced on 22 April.

title: Iran begins stepping back from the deal
detail: A year after the US withdrawal Iran announced it would stop observing some limits; the IAEA's verification of the deal covers 16 January 2016 to 8 May 2019.
notes: Source confirms the 8 May 2019 cut-off; Iran's announcement itself not separately sourced here.

title: Iran's stock passes the deal's 300 kg cap
detail: The IAEA verified that Iran's enriched uranium stock exceeded the deal's limit of 300 kg UF6 (202.8 kg U).

title: Iran enriches above the deal's 3.67% limit
detail: The IAEA verified that Iran was enriching uranium above 3.67%.

title: Khamenei: building and stockpiling bombs is wrong
detail: 'Both building and stockpiling it is wrong, as using it is haram,' Khamenei said of nuclear weapons.
notes: See fatwa.csv.

title: Iran's 'fifth step': no limit on centrifuge numbers
detail: Iran's government said it would no longer observe the deal's last key operational limit, on the number of centrifuges, while continuing to cooperate with the IAEA.

title: Explosion hits Natanz centrifuge assembly building
detail: A blast and fire damaged an above-ground building where Iran made advanced centrifuges; Iran's atomic agency later called it sabotage.
notes: Iran later said Pickaxe Mountain construction would replace this building.

title: Mohsen Fakhrizadeh killed near Tehran
detail: Iran's defence ministry said the head of its research organisation, named by Israel as father of the weapons programme, was killed in an attack in Absard.
notes: Iran blamed Israel.

title: Iran resumes 20% enrichment at Fordow
detail: Under a new parliamentary law Iran began making uranium enriched up to 20% in six cascades at Fordow.
notes: Law passed by parliament on 2 December 2020.

title: IAEA verifies Iran's first uranium metal
detail: The IAEA verified 3.6 g of natural uranium metal made at Isfahan's fuel plate plant on 6 February.
notes: Uranium metal production was banned under the deal; enriched (20%) metal followed later in 2021.

title: Intelligence minister: 'a cornered cat' may act differently
detail: Mahmoud Alavi said the fatwa forbids nuclear weapons, but if Iran were pushed in that direction it would not be Iran's fault.
notes: See fatwa.csv.

title: Iran stops deal-mandated IAEA monitoring
detail: Iran stopped letting the IAEA carry out the deal's verification and monitoring, including the Additional Protocol; inspections since rest on its safeguards agreement only.
source_name: Congressional Research Service, IF12106 (13 October 2026), citing IAEA report of 4 June 2026
notes: CRS says February 2021; 23 Feb is the day the step took effect (not stated in CRS).

title: Vienna talks on restoring the deal begin
detail: Indirect US-Iran talks, coordinated by the EU, began in Vienna to restore the deal.
notes: Source gives April 2021 only; day 01 by convention (first session 6 April).

title: Blackout hits Natanz, called 'nuclear terrorism'
detail: A power failure struck Natanz hours after new centrifuges were started; Iran's atomic chief called it nuclear terrorism.
notes: Israeli media attributed it to Israel; no official claim.

title: US threat assessment: no key weapons work
detail: The 2021 assessment said Iran was not currently undertaking the key weapons-development activities needed to produce a nuclear device, while expanding work that would bring it closer to fissile material.
notes: Release dated 9 or 13 April 2021 in different sources.

title: Iran begins enriching to 60%
detail: The IAEA verified that Iran had begun producing uranium enriched up to 60% at the Natanz pilot plant.
notes: Iran notified intent 13 April; IAEA verified 17 April.

title: Attack on Karaj centrifuge-parts workshop
detail: Iran said an Israeli sabotage operation hit the TESA Karaj workshop; one of four IAEA cameras was destroyed.
notes: IAEA called it apparent sabotage; Israel did not comment.

title: US threat assessment: no key weapons work
detail: 'We continue to assess that Iran is not currently undertaking the key nuclear weapons-development activities that we judge would be necessary to produce a nuclear device.'

title: EU tables 'final text' to restore the deal
detail: EU foreign-policy chief Borrell said what could be negotiated had been; no deal followed.
notes: Talks lapsed in September 2022.

title: US threat assessment: no key weapons work
detail: 'Iran is not currently undertaking the key nuclear weapons-development activities that would be necessary to produce a testable nuclear device.'
notes: Same sentence in 2022 ATA (7 Feb 2022) and 2024 ATA.

title: IAEA finds particles enriched to 83.7% at Fordow
detail: Samples taken on 22 January 2023 at Fordow showed particles of up to 83.7%; Iran attributed them to fluctuations, and the IAEA later said this was not inconsistent with Iran's explanation.
source_name: IAEA, GOV/2023/9 (4 March 2023), referring to GOV/2023/8
notes: First reported in GOV/2023/8 (28 Feb 2023), not fetched; IAEA later found no accumulation above 60%.

title: AP: Iran digging deep under Pickaxe Mountain near Natanz
detail: Satellite photos showed Iran tunnelling into Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La beside Natanz, possibly 80-100 m deep; Iran said it would replace the centrifuge workshop hit in 2020.
notes: Original AP report about 22 May 2023; construction began 2020 (CSIS).

title: US threat assessment: no testable-device work, but better positioned
detail: Iran is not undertaking key weapons-development work, but has 'undertaken activities that better position it to produce a nuclear device, if it chooses to do so.'
notes: CRS (Oct 2026): the 'not currently undertaking' phrase is absent from later 2024 and 2025 ODNI assessments.

title: Khamenei adviser Kharrazi: doctrine could change
detail: Kamal Kharrazi said Iran had no decision to build a bomb but would have no choice but to change its doctrine if its existence were threatened.
notes: See fatwa.csv.

title: ODNI: stock enough for 'more than a dozen' weapons
detail: A November 2024 ODNI report said Iran's fissile material, if further enriched, would be enough for more than a dozen nuclear weapons.
source_name: Congressional Research Service, IF12106 (13 October 2026), citing ODNI report of November 2024
notes: Month only; day 01 by convention. ODNI report itself not fetched.

title: Iran sharply raises 60% output at Fordow
detail: The IAEA reported Iran had begun feeding 20% uranium into linked IR-6 cascades at Fordow, raising 60% output from about 4.7 kg to more than 34 kg a month.
source_name: Institute for Science and International Security (on IAEA report of 6 Dec 2024)
notes: From the site's Iran war tracker events; IAEA report itself not fetched.

title: Trump restores 'maximum pressure' (NSPM-2)
detail: A presidential memorandum set the policy that Iran be denied a nuclear weapon and ordered a campaign to drive its oil exports to zero and to pursue UN snapback.

title: US: Iran not building a weapon, pressure on Khamenei
detail: 'We continue to assess Iran is not building a nuclear weapon and that Khamenei has not reauthorized the nuclear weapons program he suspended in 2003, though pressure has probably built on him to do so.'
notes: DNI Gabbard gave this assessment to the Senate (25 Mar) and House (26 Mar) intelligence committees.

title: US-Iran talks open in Muscat
detail: Envoy Witkoff and Foreign Minister Araghchi held a first round, mediated by Oman; four more rounds followed in Rome and Muscat to 23 May, and a sixth set for 15 June was overtaken by war.
notes: From the Iran war tracker events (talks_round rows).

title: IAEA: 60% stock reaches 408.6 kg
detail: The IAEA reported Iran's stock of uranium enriched up to 60% at 408.6 kg as of 17 May 2025, up 133.8 kg since February.

title: IAEA Board finds Iran in non-compliance
detail: For the first time in about 20 years the Board found Iran in breach of its safeguards obligations (19 for, 3 against, 11 abstentions).

title: Iran announces a third enrichment site
detail: After the Board vote Iran said it would open a new enrichment facility at a 'secure location'; it notified the IAEA the same day, but the agency has never been able to visit it.
notes: Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP). The IAEA does not know its precise whereabouts.

title: Israel strikes Natanz and nuclear scientists (Rising Lion)
detail: Israel launched Operation Rising Lion, striking Natanz, missile sites and commanders and killing nuclear scientists; strikes on Isfahan, Arak and Tehran sites followed until 24 June.
notes: From the Iran war tracker events. Iran's 60% stock was 440.9 kg that day (IAEA).

title: Israel strikes Arak heavy-water reactor
detail: Israeli strikes hit the Arak (Khondab) heavy-water reactor under construction; the IAEA confirmed damage.

title: Gabbard: Iran could make a weapon in 'weeks to months'
detail: After Trump said she was wrong, the DNI said US intelligence showed Iran could produce a weapon within weeks to months if it decided to finalise the assembly.
notes: A shift in wording from her March testimony.

title: US bombs Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan (Midnight Hammer)
detail: Seven B-2 bombers dropped 14 bunker-busters on Fordow and Natanz and a submarine fired cruise missiles at Isfahan.
notes: US time 21 June evening; Iran time 22 June. From the Iran war tracker events.

title: Israel-Iran ceasefire ends the 12-day war
detail: Trump announced a ceasefire mediated with Qatar; it took hold on 24 June.
notes: From the Iran war tracker events.

title: Iran suspends cooperation with the IAEA
detail: President Pezeshkian signed a law making inspector access subject to the Supreme National Security Council; inspectors left Iran on 4 July.
notes: From the Iran war tracker events.

title: Britain, France and Germany trigger snapback
detail: The E3 notified the Security Council of Iran's significant non-performance, starting a 30-day clock to restore UN sanctions.

title: Cairo framework on resuming inspections
detail: Iran and the IAEA signed a framework in Cairo on resuming inspections; Iran said no access was granted yet.
notes: Iran declared it void on 20 November 2025 after a Board resolution.

title: 71 MPs urge review of defence doctrine
detail: A letter from 71 of 290 MPs asked the security council to reassess doctrine, arguing that possessing nuclear weapons for deterrence would not breach the fatwa on their use.
notes: Government did not comment. See fatwa.csv.

title: UN sanctions restored (snapback)
detail: UN sanctions from Resolutions 1696 to 1929 returned at 00:00 GMT on 28 September after the Council declined to continue relief.
notes: 20:00 ET 27 Sept. The IAEA (GOV/2026/8) cites the resolutions as applying from 28 Sept 2025.

title: EU re-imposes nuclear sanctions
detail: The EU Council re-imposed the UN-derived and its own nuclear-related sanctions lifted under the deal.
notes: Also Regulation (EU) 2025/1975 and Decision 2025/1978 (listings).

title: Iran declares the 2015 deal terminated
detail: On the deal's scheduled termination day Iran declared the JCPOA and all its restrictions ended.
notes: From the Iran war tracker events.

title: IAEA Board demands accounting; Iran ends Cairo deal
detail: The Board demanded information on Iran's enriched uranium and bombed sites (GOV/2025/71); Iran declared the Cairo framework terminated.
notes: From the Iran war tracker events.

title: Executive order: tariffs on Iran's trading partners
detail: Executive Order 14382 authorised an additional tariff, for example 25%, on goods from any country that buys goods or services from Iran.
notes: Effective 7 February 2026.

title: US-Iran talks resume in Muscat
detail: Witkoff, Kushner and CENTCOM's commander held indirect talks with Araghchi through Omani mediators; rounds in Geneva followed on 17 and 26 February.
notes: From the Iran war tracker events.

title: Witkoff: Iran 'probably a week away' from bomb material
detail: The US envoy said Iran's enrichment was up to 60% and it was probably a week from industrial-grade bomb-making material; experts disputed it given Iran's damaged facilities.
notes: Said on air 21 Feb. See breakout_estimates.csv.

title: Third Geneva round, with IAEA chief present
detail: The US reportedly demanded the destruction of Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan and the handover of all enriched uranium; Oman reported progress and planned technical talks.
notes: From the Iran war tracker events. The planned Vienna technical talks never took place.

title: IAEA cannot verify stock or enrichment suspension
detail: The IAEA said that without access it could give no information on the size or whereabouts of Iran's enriched uranium; its last figure was 440.9 kg of 60% uranium as of 13 June 2025.
notes: IAEA observed vehicle activity at the Isfahan tunnel entrance where 20% and 60% material was stored (para 19).

title: US-Israeli war begins; Supreme Leader Khamenei killed
detail: Israel and the United States launched a war on Iran; Ali Khamenei was killed in a strike on his compound on the first day.
notes: Iranian state media confirmed on 1 March. Israel's name: Operation Roaring Lion; US: Operation Epic Fury.

title: IAEA confirms damage at Natanz enrichment plant entrances
detail: The IAEA confirmed from satellite imagery recent damage to entrance buildings of the underground Natanz plant, with no radiological consequence.
notes: On 2 March Grossi had said there was no sign any nuclear facility was hit. Natanz was hit again around 21 March.

title: Mojtaba Khamenei becomes Supreme Leader
detail: The Assembly of Experts named Ali Khamenei's son Mojtaba as his successor; he has not said publicly whether he upholds his father's fatwa.
notes: Date: 8 March per Wikipedia; the site's tracker notes the Assembly met 7-9 March. See fatwa.csv.

title: Araghchi: enriched uranium is 'under the rubble'
detail: The foreign minister said Iran's enriched uranium lay under the rubble of the June 2025 strikes and Iran had no plan to recover it.

title: US threat assessment: enrichment 'obliterated', monitoring leaders
detail: ODNI said enrichment was obliterated in 2025 with no effort to rebuild it, and it was watching whether current or new leaders would authorise a weapons programme.
source_name: ODNI press release on 2026 Annual Threat Assessment (18 March 2026)
notes: The ATA itself does not address weapons activities (CRS). Information cut-off 14 March 2026.

title: Khondab heavy-water plant knocked out
detail: The IAEA said the heavy-water production plant at Khondab (Arak) was severely damaged and no longer operational; it held no declared nuclear material.
source_name: American Nuclear Society Nuclear Newswire, 6 April 2026 (IAEA updates)
notes: Ardakan yellowcake plant also reported attacked 27 Mar; strikes near Bushehr reactor 18 Mar and 4 Apr.

title: IAEA: stock size and location unknown; Isfahan tunnels named
detail: The IAEA said it could not report the size, location or form of Iran's enriched uranium, identified the Isfahan tunnels as a storage site and said verification in Iran stopped after 28 February.
source_name: Institute for Science and International Security, analysis of IAEA reports of 4 June 2026
notes: IAEA report itself not fetched. From the Iran war tracker events.

title: US-Iran memorandum: Iran 'shall not procure or develop' weapons
detail: A memorandum to end the war says Iran reaffirms it shall not procure or develop nuclear weapons, with stockpiled material to be resolved, at minimum by downblending under IAEA supervision.
notes: Conflict: signed electronically on Sunday 14 June (Vance and Ghalibaf), then by Trump and Pezeshkian on 17 June.

title: Iran suspends its commitments under the memorandum
detail: Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi announced Iran was suspending its commitments under the memorandum.
notes: Weak source; primary Iranian statement not retrieved. From the Iran war tracker events.

title: Treasury launches 'Operation Economic Outcast'
detail: Treasury Secretary Bessent set deadlines for countries to halt economic activity with Iran or lose access to the dollar system, with secondary sanctions in five sectors.
notes: Treasury's own press release not found.

title: CSIS: record construction at Pickaxe Mountain
detail: Satellite imagery showed more road activity in 2026 than at any point in the site's history and hardened tunnel portals, but no sign the site can yet enrich.
notes: Construction began 2020; CSIS's September 2025 baseline showed a finished perimeter fence and faster digging.

title: IAEA Board reports Iran to the Security Council
detail: The Board adopted a resolution reporting Iran's non-compliance to the Security Council (23-3, 8 abstentions).
source_name: UK government, statement on the resolution (September 2026)
notes: GOV/2026/61. From the Iran war tracker events.

title: Pezeshkian: 'Developing nuclear weapons is haram'
detail: The president said Iran was not trying to build a weapon and would let inspectors in, with details for negotiation.
notes: See fatwa.csv.

title: Trump on Pickaxe Mountain: 'we may have to go there'
detail: Trump said the US might strike the Pickaxe Mountain site and would 'knock it out fast'.
notes: From the Iran war tracker events; repeated 31 October.

title: Foreign ministry: changing nuclear doctrine 'a real issue'
detail: Spokesman Baghaei said revising the doctrine was a real issue because the US and Israel had killed the man who issued the fatwa; the security council chief said no decision had been taken.
notes: See fatwa.csv for the October-November 2026 debate.

title: Iran sends nuclear proposal through Qatar
detail: Iran sent a formal nuclear proposal through Qatari mediators, with further talks tied to its seven demands, Reuters reported.
source_name: CBS News live updates (citing Reuters), 5 November 2026
notes: From the Iran war tracker events.
